options.plan: Free; organization offer documented, account entitlement unverified
options.region: No Cloud region selected; storage destinations not verified
options.configuration: Vendor-owned project; customer org grants and cross-org role assignments; app-owned tenant access; no SCIM bridge

conditions: Use a vendor-owned project and explicit grants to customer organizations, with bounded project roles and individual user role assignments. Configure the consuming application's tenant model separately; this is an IAM organization design, not implemented SaaS tenancy.

The Free offer at https://zitadel.com/pricing advertises unlimited organizations within usage quotas; reconcile administrator, API and account limits before source approval. The B2B guide's scalability language is not unlimited usage, a tested entitlement or a future zero-cost guarantee.

Business roles require application-side authorization; IAM manager roles are separate. No customer provisioning, enterprise connection, protocol/client compatibility, auditability, security-control or production isolation was verified. Cloud sources are mutable and dated, not release-pinned.

evidence.summary: The B2B guide describes customer organizations, shared projects and bounded grants/role assignments. Proposed SUPPORTED is conditional B2B application context, not a complete identity/lifecycle solution or verified Cloud Free account.

conditions: Model a vendor-owned portal project with separately granted partner organizations and explicit per-user roles. A portal's business admin role must not silently become ORG_OWNER, PROJECT_OWNER or a catalog-curator role.

The Next.js example uses a server-held client secret and a service-account PAT for management reads; it is not a public SPA/mobile compatibility proof or a production credential-handling prescription. Minimize management permissions and verify every selected partner organization server-side before exposing data or assignments.

Review Free-plan usage and management limits separately. The example's broad grants and development settings are not secure production defaults; portal onboarding, privileged writes, session revocation and tenant-isolation acceptance were not tested or implemented.

evidence.summary: The server-side B2B portal example displays granted projects and organization-bound user roles. Proposed SUPPORTED retains application authorization, management credentials and account-limit prerequisites; the sample was not executed.

conditions: Represent each intended customer boundary with an explicit organization-to-application-tenant mapping and vendor-project grant. Limit delegated roles; an organization's IAM data separation does not prove isolation of the consuming SaaS database, APIs or sessions.

An organization scope or domain discovery can route login settings, but routing alone does not authorize the selected application tenant. Validate current subject, project/grant and selected tenant on the server; do not trust a browser-selected organization ID, email domain or branding as permission.

No live multi-organization configuration or cross-tenant negative test was performed. Residency, population/client compatibility, hierarchical tenancy, lifecycle enforcement and organization management entitlement remain unverified.

evidence.summary: The organization guide describes multiple organizations in one instance and delegated project access. Proposed SUPPORTED concerns configurable IAM organization context, not observed application resource isolation or verified Free-plan management rights.

conditions: Keep one home organization for the identity record, while external user role assignments grant that same identity access to projects in other organizations. Project grants delegate role management; individual role assignments authorize users. Neither creates a second home identity record.

For application memberships, bind the stable subject to each explicit tenant/project/grant context and validate access when switching tenants and on subsequent requests. Login organization and identity resource owner are not substitutes for the selected application's membership authorization.

Per https://zitadel.com/docs/guides/manage/console/users-overview, equal email addresses can belong to different accounts and users remain in one home organization; do not merge identities by email or infer native user migration. Grant removal, offboarding, cached claims and existing local sessions need separate enforcement tests.

This proposes cross-organization application access using role assignments, not multiple native user owners, arbitrary SaaS membership synchronization, SCIM Group transport or verified lifecycle behavior. Free account/API/admin entitlement and live acceptance remain unresolved.

evidence.summary: External user role assignments allow one identity to access projects across tenant organizations, independently of project-grant delegation. Proposed SUPPORTED is conditional application membership context, not multiple home organizations or automatic SaaS access enforcement.
